ledger.claim: Route deviation is established on this trip's own trace. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 18.0 km against a booked optimal of 10.0 km: an excess of 8.0 km and 80%. POL-RD-01 requires both establishment tests to pass, and both do (excess greater than 20% of optimal, and greater than 0.8 km absolute). Under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs the threshold test and trip_record.actual_distance_km may not be cited for it; the two happen to agree here at 18.0 km, but the finding rests on the GPS artifact.

The computed deviation status is additionally MATERIAL: 80% of optimal exceeds the 50% material threshold in POL-RD-01 (the absolute 8.0 km limb is not additionally needed once the percentage limb fires). Materiality under POL-RD-01 is assessed on the excess REMAINING after adjustment, and even after the closure adjustment below the remaining excess of 4.4 km still exceeds both establishment tests against the adjusted optimal of 13.6 km. A material deviation also requires the driver_profile check in POL-RD-06.

The LTA closure advisory exonerates the driver only up to the POL-RD-03 cap, and the cap bites hard here. The advisory names the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, a segment the booked optimal route traverses, and its window 18:14-18:55 covers the whole trip, so the exoneration is engaged. The justified excess is the lesser of the measured 8.0 km or 1.30 x (shortest lawful alternative 12.0 km - booked optimal 10.0 km) + 1.00 km tolerance = 3.60 km. So 3.60 km is exonerated and the remaining 4.4 km of excess is not, and is refundable under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal of 13.6 km.

The driver did not merely take the diversion the closure required. The advisory itself records the shortest lawful route between the booked endpoints as 12.0 km, while the vehicle covered 18.0 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff: 6.0 km further than the lawful alternative and 4.4 km further than even the capped exoneration allows. POL-RD-03 caps exoneration on ADDITIONAL distance for exactly this reason - a closure explanation cannot be stretched to cover any distance a driver chooses to run.

Running POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route gives the refund arithmetically. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.6 + 0.28 x 27.2) x surge 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP on the optimal route = 23.416. Refund = charged_total 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, and the payable figure rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 is 8.05. The adjusted duration of 27.2 minutes is the booked 20.0 minutes scaled by 13.6/10.0, as POL-RD-03 requires.

The refund is neither de minimis nor a full-refund case, and the figure returns the whole of the sum the rider contests. 8.004 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and it is 25.5% of charged_total, far below the 90% at which POL-RD-02 would escalate the remedy. The result is a partial refund of SGD 8.05 - which is exactly the SGD 8.05 amount_contested_sgd, so the rider is made whole on the sum in dispute.

The 2.80 charged at the off-route 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is already comprehended in the 8.05 figure and I do not ask for it on top. The recomputed fare carries only the 1.00 gantry lying on the optimal route (Pelton lawful diversion entry, on_optimal_route true); the 2.80 line is off the optimal route and is therefore already excluded by the POL-RD-02 recomputation. Under POL-RD-09 such charges are itemised separately for transparency but must NEVER be added to the POL-RD-02 figure, and adding them would double-count the same money.

The trace on which this claim rests is unimpaired, so no corroboration requirement and no escalation is engaged. It carries 205 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval over 100.0% coverage, with zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires, so excess is measured from the trace itself, the claim does not need an independent source under POL-RD-07(ii), and POL-RD-10(3) is not triggered.

The rider's POL-RD-08 burden is discharged. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-09113 with a consistent timeline (trip started 18:20:00 against a first fix at 18:20:00), and the excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold is measured from the unimpaired trace. The rider's own claim history does not add the extra corroboration requirement at the end of POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so that factor is simply not engaged.

The driver cannot shift the unexcused excess onto the rider as a rider-requested detour. The only rider message in the chat log is 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion'; it names no road or place and carries waypoint_hint null, so under POL-RD-04 the corroboration test is undecidable on the record, the clause is unavailable, and the case is decided on the remaining clauses. Even read at face value, that instruction authorised the LAWFUL diversion - which the advisory fixes at 12.0 km - not 18.0 km of driving.

The POL-RD-06 driver_profile check was run and returns no repeat pattern, and I state that frankly rather than assert one. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 610 completed trips in 90 days, so neither limb of the pattern test is met (3 or more flags; or a ratio of 0.05 or more with at least 40 trips). No FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) follow, and the remedy remains the POL-RD-02 arithmetic of SGD 8.05.

No relocation clause applies, so the booked optimal of 10.0 km (as adjusted under POL-RD-03) is the correct baseline and no longer 'amended' route may be substituted for it. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 is not triggered at all and the driver cannot manufacture a larger baseline out of an amendment that never happened.

The closure on this route is on file, not merely asserted. LTA advisory ADV-20260920-113 records an emergency resurfacing closure of the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector — the very segment the booked optimal route used, as trip_record.optimal_route_source names it — with a validity window of 18:14 to 18:55 on 20 September 2026 that overlaps the trip (intersects_route true, overlaps_trip_window true), and the shortest lawful alternative between the booked endpoints was 12.0 km. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is therefore the lesser of the measured 8.0 km and 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00 = 3.60 km. So 3.60 km of the excess is exonerated, the closure-adjusted optimal route is 13.60 km and 27.2 minutes, and only the remaining 4.40 km is a deviation the driver must answer for.

POL-RD-03(c) is satisfied on this record rather than assumed. The fare_breakdown places the vehicle on the off-optimal Industrial loop exit gantry at 18:42 — a corridor the optimal route does not use — and the trip completes at the booked dropoff, so the route leaves the Pelton corridor before the closed segment and rejoins it after. The driver's account is corroborated contemporaneously: at 18:22:40 he told the rider the Pelton Canal Link closure was sending traffic around the industrial loop, and at 18:23:10 the rider replied, in terms, that the driver should take the lawful diversion. The rider's own filed claim opens by accepting the road closure, so this is not a bare uncited traffic excuse of the kind POL-RD-13 is aimed at — a real advisory covering the trip window is on file and the driver discharges his POL-RD-08 burden by naming a specific artifact (the advisory) and a specific clause (POL-RD-03).

POL-RD-02 run against the closure-adjusted optimal route produces the driver's floor and no more: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 of ERP on the optimal route = 23.416. Charged_total is 31.42, so the refund is 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to 8.05. That is above the 0.50 de minimis, and at 25.5 per cent of charged_total it is far below the 90 per cent that would force a FULL_REFUND. The same arithmetic run on the unadjusted booked optimal would produce 12.75, so the closure exoneration is worth SGD 4.70 to the driver and the rider's recovery ends at 8.05.

Once the closure exoneration is applied, the excess remaining is 4.40 km — 44 per cent of the 10.0 km booked optimal and 4.40 km in absolute terms — so on POL-RD-01's own words, which require materiality to be assessed on the excess remaining after adjustment, this deviation is established but not MATERIAL and the POL-RD-06 machinery is not engaged at all: no uplift and no referral. Even if the tribunal measures materiality on the unadjusted 8.0 km / 80 per cent figure the derived status field records, the check returns clean in any event — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610, so neither the three-flag test nor the 0.05 ratio test (0 / 610 = 0) is met. Those are the only two profile fields POL-RD-06 names, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

The SGD 2.80 Industrial loop exit gantry is flagged off the optimal route (on_optimal_route false) and is deliberately excluded from the recomputed fare, so it is already comprehended inside the 8.05 refund. POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding it on top; the anti-double-count rule exists precisely so that a 31.42 charge carrying 2.80 of off-route ERP does not yield both a distance refund and a second ERP refund.

The SGD 1.00 Pelton lawful diversion entry line is a properly chargeable pass-through, not a phantom charge: the fare_breakdown flags it on_optimal_route true and the trip_record carries optimal_route_erp_sgd of 1.00, so the line has a counterpart in the record and is not a charge line with no counterpart anywhere in the gps_trace or trip_record of the kind POL-RD-10(8) escalates.

The case is ruleable on this record and no POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The gps_trace carries 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval with 100 per cent coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec of 0, so POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) are not met and no gap-handling or corroboration consequence arises; the trip identifier TRP-09113 is identical on the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown; no artifact's timestamps run backwards; the computed refund of 8.05 is below both the SGD 150.00 ceiling and charged_total; and every artifact the driver relies on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so no POL-GEN-02 discount is owed and the confidence cap a sub-1.0 deciding artifact would impose does not arise. Escalation would hold the disputed 8.05 without resolving anything this trace does not already resolve.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — this is a partial refund.

Agreed and on the record: an LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-09113-01) closed the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, the segment the booked optimal route used, from 18:14 to 18:55 on 20 September 2026, covering this trip, and it records the shortest lawful alternative between the booked endpoints as 12.0 km. The driver took the signed industrial diversion and told the rider at 18:22:40; the rider replied at 18:23:10, 'please take the lawful diversion.'

1. Deviation established (POL-RD-01). The GPS trace governs: 18.0 km (EV-GPS-09113 trace_distance_km) against the booked optimal of 10.0 km (EV-TRIP-09113) is an excess of 8.0 km and 80%, passing both tests. The trip_record's rounded copy happens to agree; that does not change which field decides.

2. The closure excuses only part of it (POL-RD-03). The advisory names a road the optimal route traverses and its window covers the trip, so the driver is exonerated — but the exoneration is capped at the lesser of the measured excess (8.0 km) and 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00 = 3.60 km. So 3.60 km is excused and 4.40 km is not. The closure-adjusted optimal is 10.0 + 3.60 = 13.60 km, and its duration is 20.0 x 13.60/10.0 = 27.2 min. The driver's claim to that effect is accepted; the rider's point that 18.0 km exceeds even the 12.0 km lawful alternative is also accepted — it is exactly why the cap bites.

3. The refund is arithmetic (POL-RD-02). recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (EV-FARE-09113), + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP on the optimal route = 23.416. Charged_total is 31.42 (EV-FARE-09113). Refund = 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and 25.5% of charged_total, far below the 90% that would force a full refund.

4. The off-route gantry is not added again (POL-RD-09(1)). The SGD 2.80 charged at the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry, which is off the optimal route, is already comprehended inside the SGD 8.05, exactly as both sides say; adding it would double-count the same money.

5. One fare line is a billing error (POL-RD-09(4)). The SGD 1.00 charged at the 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' gantry is a charge for a gantry this trip's GPS trace never passes: of the 205 fixes, the nearest comes 834.18 m from the gantry, well outside the 250 m match radius the clause prescribes. The driver's claim that this line is 'properly chargeable' and 'not a phantom charge' is rejected: the on_optimal_route flag and trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd show the line has a counterpart in the record, which answers POL-RD-10(8) escalation, but neither shows the vehicle actually crossed the gantry, which is what POL-RD-09(4) asks. The SGD 1.00 is refunded in full as a standalone correction, and the line is referred for billing-integrity review.

6. No repeat-deviation uplift, no conduct referral (POL-RD-06, POL-GEN-01). driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610 — the trailing-window counters the clause names, not the lifetime prior_deviation_flags. Neither limb of the pattern test is met. (Materiality is assessed on the excess remaining after adjustment, 4.40 km, which is 32% of the 13.60 km adjusted optimal and below the 8.0 km absolute limb, so the deviation is established but not material; even on the unadjusted 80% the profile check returns clean, so nothing turns on it. The rider's assertion of materiality is corrected on that basis.)

7. No rider-requested detour (POL-RD-04). The rider's message names no road or place and carries waypoint_hint null, so the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable; in any event the instruction authorised only the 12.0 km lawful diversion, not 18.0 km.

8. No escalation (POL-RD-10). The trace is unimpaired — 205 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, maximum gap 0.0 s — so POL-RD-07 limbs (a)-(c) and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged; the identifier TRP-09113 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the refund is below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total; and the only fare line without a trace crossing is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes.

9. No relocation (POL-RD-05): pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so the booked optimal, as adjusted by POL-RD-03, is the baseline.

Outcome: the SGD 8.05 you contested is returned in full, and SGD 1.00 more is returned as the billing correction — SGD 9.05 in total. Confidence is 0.90; the deciding facts are carried by artifacts all at weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-09113, EV-TRIP-09113, EV-FARE-09113 and EV-ADVIS-09113-01), so the cap is 1.0, and no POL-GEN-02 discount applies.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' ERP line charges a gantry this trip's gps_trace never passes (nearest of the 205 fixes is 834.18 m from the gantry, outside POL-RD-09(4)'s 250 m match radius); the line has been refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction and is referred for billing-integrity review.
